idiom_name: discriminated-union approval states + server-side guard comparing the approver to the stored initiator
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds a type-level model of the workflow: a discriminated union ({ status: 'pending'; initiatedBy: UserId } | { status: 'approved'; initiatedBy: UserId; approvedBy: UserId }) with exhaustive switch handling makes it impossible to read approvedBy off a pending request, and the compiler flags every transition that forgets a state (the narrowing behaviour the handbook describes). The enforcement is still server-side: the guard or middleware performing the approval must compare the authenticated principal's id with the stored initiatedBy, and the state transition must be a conditional or transactional write, because types are erased at runtime and any client can call the endpoint directly. What replaces the classic role object is the union type for the data plus the authorization guard for the rule; neither is provided by the language.
pitfalls: Type-level states are erased at runtime: the service must re-check status and identity; a client can POST the approve endpoint directly, bypassing every type.
initiatedBy/approvedBy must be assigned on the server from the verified session or token; if the client supplies them, the distinctness comparison is meaningless.
as/any casts and JSON.parse reintroduce states the union forbids; validate with a schema at the boundary before feeding values into the workflow.
